topic: Under an exact stable quantile-span distributional synthetic-control model with fixed donor and period counts, smooth pre-period laws with a uniformly strong sum-zero Gram, simplex-constrained weight estimation from n observations per pre cell, and finite-support post-period laws estimated from m independent observations per cell, derive the exact separately anchored signed endpoint energy for discrete quantile errors and the constrained-Gaussian pre-weight quadratic. Prove the joint expansion and its three n/sqrt(m) phase laws, including local m^(-1/2) knot offsets, n^(-1/2) simplex-face offsets, cross-term control, and necessary-and-sufficient component degeneracy conditions. Construct feasible simultaneous L2 QTE confidence balls with uniform coverage and diameter order n^(-1/2)+m^(-1/4), oracle calibration only on separated regular strata, and a certified conditional minimax common-cutoff calculation near collisions/faces. Prove the unavoidable honesty penalty rather than claiming oracle adaptation. The same-question consumer is Zhai et al.'s discrete mosquito-abundance distributional synthetic-control analysis, excluding its separate binary CDF/W1 estimator. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Separately anchored endpoint algebra, tangent-cone weight limits, cross-term bounds and all three phases are derived; within-cell local offsets are asymptotically observed while cross-cell translations and face offsets remain nuisance; a one-dimensional Bernoulli calculation certifies the least stable 95% squared-radius cutoff in (1.913,1.914], versus collision oracle 1.385903824, and finite-sample DKW balls attain the target diameter order. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove one measurable certified nuisance-region/cluster procedure attains the conditional local minimax cutoff while retaining uniform coverage across changing supports, covariance ranks and simplex faces, with oracle calibration on separated regular strata. EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the specified two-donor Gaussian calibration problem with a weight at h/sqrt(n), bounded face/cross-cell knot offsets, and certified probability enclosures; add a within-cell mass of order m^(-1/2) and require the procedure to learn its internal offset, retain coverage, and converge to the conditional cutoff with vanishing fallback probability. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/panel_dsc_jump_energy_phase.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct a measurable, certified nuisance-region and support/face-clustering procedure for fixed-donor finite-support distributional synthetic control that gives honest simultaneous L2 QTE balls across collisions, covariance-rank changes, and simplex faces while recovering oracle cutoffs only on separated regular strata?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest published inferential components occupy disjoint regimes: Alvarez–Orestes regularize DSC through smooth continuous quantiles and dilution over a growing donor pool; Chernozhukov et al. handle discrete QTE inversion without estimated simplex weights; and Canen–Song handle simplex faces without a nonsmooth post-period quantile map. The banked conditional-Wasserstein run separately left observable multiplier consistency open through degeneracy, while the proxy-effect-law run shows that collision-aware positive-measure repair requires uniform merge/split control. The first proof step must therefore build one total Borel partition from empirical CDF and Gram information that jointly indexes signed endpoint energies and tangent cones; a clustering error can change both anchors and cone dimension, so measurability, fallback control, and conditional cutoff consistency cannot be proved separately.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem specifying an implementable cluster/nuisance-region algorithm and cutoff functional, proving uniform simultaneous 1-alpha L2 coverage, diameter O(n^(-1/2)+m^(-1/4)), o(1) fallback probability, conditional local-minimax calibration on collision/face strata, and oracle calibration exactly under stated separation conditions.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published DSC work supplies identification and broad rates, while regular quantile-mixture inference assumes positive densities and many diluted controls. Finite-space Wasserstein theory supplies a directional derivative for a different transport functional. Here the first proof step is the local expansion: one-dimensional quantile loss must be decomposed into separately anchored signed endpoint contributions before combination with projection of the pre-period Gaussian score onto a moving simplex tangent cone. The relative n and sqrt(m) scales create three limits, and neither the Wasserstein linear-program derivative nor boundary M-estimation alone identifies the cross term or necessary-and-sufficient degeneracy conditions. The prompt's presolve derivation is explicitly unverified, so resolution must validate rather than assume it.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint weak-convergence theorem giving the explicit separately anchored signed endpoint energy and constrained-Gaussian quadratic in all three n/sqrt(m) regimes, uniform cross-term remainders under local knot and face offsets, and algebraic necessary-and-sufficient conditions for degeneracy of each component.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation and exact quantile-span formulation are the natural baseline for explaining why fixed-donor discrete sampling changes inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove a directional Hadamard derivative of a finite-support transport value and apply the directional delta method while tracking ordinary-bootstrap failure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest proof template for an atomic transport/quantile loss, though the DSC proof must replace the random LP value by separately anchored endpoint energies.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a local quadratic expansion and minimize the Gaussian limit over the parameter-space tangent cone.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the geometric move required for the simplex-constrained pre-weight quadratic.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply a directional functional delta method and derivative-aware resampling, with a necessity result for ordinary-bootstrap failure under nonlinear Gaussian derivatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint and cone maps are directionally but not fully differentiable at collisions and faces.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Active-rank chi-square calibration and conditional Gaussian nuisance elimination transfer only partway. The destination loss sums a cone-projected Gaussian quadratic and a signed endpoint-energy term whose law changes with local knot offsets and with whether a within-cell mass perturbation is statistically observed. The banked donor-face project solved a score-only experiment only by observing the effect coordinate without noise, and its reviewers demanded a worked multi-face Gaussian program. The first proof step must instead formulate the correct Gaussian/multinomial product experiment and its face-coherent target map; active-rank selection alone does not remove the endpoint nuisance, while unconditional worst-case calibration forfeits the desired conditional cutoff.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit measurable acceptance-region rule and interval-certified cutoff map for the two-donor Gaussian-multinomial experiment, with a least-favorable nuisance characterization, uniform 95% coverage over bounded face and knot offsets, consistent learning of the within-cell offset, and vanishing fallback probability.

open_problems.why_unsolved: General adaptive-confidence-set theory shows that oracle behavior is available only when strata are statistically distinguishable, but its strata are smoothness classes rather than collision patterns, covariance ranks, and simplex faces. The banked tie-boundary project similarly left its matching union-honest upper interval and exact frontier open. For DSC, the first lower-bound step must replace function-class packings or max-of-means perturbations by contiguous finite-support alternatives that jointly move endpoint masses, knot locations, and a face-local weight while keeping the observation experiments indistinguishable. The n and m samples create a two-scale separation boundary, so neither existing ordered moduli nor discrete CDF-band inversion identifies the exact penalty.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching theorems giving a Le Cam, constrained-risk, or ordered-modulus lower bound for the worst-near-singular L2 radius and an attainable separated-stratum hybrid, with necessary-and-sufficient separation rates for oracle cutoff recovery in every n/sqrt(m) phase.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames honest confidence sets through the tension between adaptive centers, testing rates, and necessarily enlarged diameters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive estimators exploit simpler submodels -> confidence sets must reveal rather than merely exploit simplicity -> indistinguishable submodels force larger honest diameter -> DSC collision and face strata require a sharp distinguishability frontier

open_problems.why_unsolved: The failed close-group project established that weak convergence of a reduced statistic does not transfer discontinuous coverage or unbounded diameter loss, and that an exact-coordinate Gaussian reduction can change the minimax problem. In DSC, the first proof step must derive joint local asymptotic behavior for empirical cell masses, moving knot locations, and the simplex-constrained weight estimator, then supply boundary-null and uniform-integrability controls that survive changes of support cluster and face. A pointwise expansion, even if the presolve algebra is correct, does not by itself justify the claimed conditional local-minimax cutoff in the original sampling experiment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A localized deficiency-equivalence theorem, or matching asymptotic-minimax lower- and upper-transfer lemmas, on compact face/knot nuisance sets with uniform coverage-event boundary control and uniform integrability for squared-radius loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian-experiment conditional inference with an unrestricted functional nuisance and prove uniform asymptotic size.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The local DSC experiment likewise separates an asymptotically observed internal offset from nuisance translations that cannot be learned uniformly.

literature_map:
1. Gunsilius (2023, Econometrica, arXiv:2001.06118) defines quantile-span DSC for continuous, discrete, and mixed laws, but does not deliver honest simultaneous QTE balls.
2. Chen (2020, Journal of Applied Econometrics, DOI 10.1002/jae.2778) gives an alternative distributional SC based on pre-period quantile residual matching and poor-fit adjustment.
3. Zhang, Zhang and Zhang (2026 revision, arXiv:2405.00953) establish DSC prediction optimality and weight convergence rates, not exact discrete local limit laws.
4. Alvarez and Orestes (2024, Quantile Mixture Models) provide formal DSC inference under smooth continuous distributions and a growing-donor dilution condition; fixed donors and atoms are excluded.
5. Zhai et al. (2026, PLOS Computational Biology, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014355) analyze discrete mosquito abundance by smoothing/interpolating quantiles and use pointwise percentile-bootstrap intervals.
6. Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, Melly and Wüthrich (2020, JASA, arXiv:1608.05142) obtain simultaneous discrete-QTE bands by projecting and inverting CDF bands.
7. Ma, Genton and Parzen (2011, AISM, DOI 10.1007/s10463-008-0215-z) show classical sample-quantile asymptotics become nonnormal with discreteness and ties, then regularize using mid-distributions.
8. Sommerfeld and Munk (2018, JRSSB, arXiv:1610.03287) derive directional-Hadamard limits for empirical Wasserstein distances on finite spaces and document ordinary-bootstrap failure.
9. Fang and Santos (2019, ReStud, arXiv:1404.3763) characterize bootstrap validity for directionally differentiable functionals and give derivative-aware inference.
10. Hong and Li (2018, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2018.06.007) develop numerical first- and second-order directional delta methods for convex Lipschitz maps.
11. Andrews (1999, Econometrica, DOI 10.1111/1468-0262.00082) supplies local quadratic and tangent-cone limit theory for extremum estimators on boundaries.
12. Canen and Song (2026 revision, arXiv:2501.15692) give uniformly valid inference for simplex-valued optimizer weights through polyhedral-cone projection, but not for post-period discrete QTEs.
13. Fang and Seo (2021, Econometrica, arXiv:1910.07689) obtain uniformly valid projection tests for convex-cone restrictions without estimating local parameter spaces.
14. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, Econometrica, arXiv:1409.6337) and Cox and Shi (2023, ReStud, arXiv:1907.06317) provide conditional-nuisance and active-rank Gaussian calibration templates.
15. Robins and van der Vaart (2006, Annals, arXiv:math/0605473) and Hoffmann and Nickl (2011, Annals, arXiv:1202.5145) show why honest confidence sets cannot generally attain oracle diameters on statistically indistinguishable strata.
